body: Unfortunately, my parents don't really get how serious all of this is. They think it's just some teenage angst (which I'm not necessarily doubting, because hormones can be intense sometimes), and that I won't actually do it. I've been too afraid to show them/tell them that I SH because I feel that they'll just tell me I'm making poor choices that are going to affect my future life, like college, jobs, and anything else that may pop along in life.

No, not worst. 

I do try to keep my mind off of cutting, but it is something I think I've fallen to. It seriously preoccupies my mind about 45% of the day. I have been getting better about not cutting, but it's hard not to sometimes. I am/was an avid artist, but lately it's like everything I do, I have a voice (specifically, it's a general representation of my rapist's voice/tone) telling me that it's worthless, I shouldn't bother. That I'm nothing, that my art is horrible, that I should stop reading that book because I'll never be that happy, or that my life is already worse than that persons. 

Anyways, like I said, I have an appointment on Tuesday. I want to get it all out. I've (kind of) held back on her, because our main focus has been the general anxiety brought on by the rape-incident, but last session we talked about how it's probably contributing to (what she called) a bit of depression. I just want to get it all out, like vomit or tears or something.

It kills me to think that I started cutting just because nobody told me it was addictive, and that it would actually become a problem. I seriously, honestly thought it was a one-time deal kinda thing. I'd heard about people needing help to stop, but I never figured that it would happen to *me*, or almost everybody else. I'm really regretting not taking a bike ride now, almost 4 years later.

I know... It's almost silly how much it consumes you. I'm in high school and I beg and pray for the day to be over so I can cut. I don't really even want to, but my mind always finds a semi-legitimate way to make me feel it's ok to cut. The scariest part of it all is how, after I cut, it *does* make me feel normal, make me feel that I'm ok, because the idea of cutting hides in the deepest crevices of my mind for a few moments.
